# Devboard task file schema (v1)

Location: `<data-root>/<repo>/<task-slug>.yaml` (or `.yml` / `.json` — same
structure). The repo grouping comes from the directory name, never from file
content. Producers should write atomically (temp file + rename). Unknown
top-level fields are rendered generically in an "Other" section — additive
extensions don't break the renderer.

Archived tasks live in `<data-root>/<repo>/_archive/` — the devboard UI
moves files there (and back) via its archive/un-archive buttons; the file
content is untouched and no schema field is involved. Producers should
write only to the repo dir, never into `_archive/`.

## Ownership (one author per field)

Worklog is the system of record; a devboard task file is disposable live
telemetry. Where both systems describe the same task, **each field has
exactly one author**, and mirroring flows worklog→devboard only. The
`worklog` binary is the privileged writer of these files — but never a
required one: a bare schema-valid file with no worklog ticket is fully
supported.

| Field | Author | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `worklog`, `title` | worklog (when ticket exists) | mirrored from the ticket; agent-authored on bare tasks |
| `type` | worklog | `epic` marks this file as an epic container; `spike` marks investigation-first work (short phase track); absent for an ordinary ticket |
| `children` | worklog (roster identity), agent (per-child in-flight detail) | see "Epic files" below |
| `links` (PR) | worklog (`worklog pr`) | other links agent-authored |
| `phase` | agent (dev-context phases) | worklog `done` sets `done` |
| `tier`, `complexity`, `branch`, `session` | agent | identity/telemetry |
| `plan`, `scorecard`, `decisions`, `code`, `needs_you`, `waiting_on` | agent | in-flight detail; deliberately NOT stored in worklog |
| notes (rendered section) | worklog (`notes/<id>.md`) | rendered live from the worklog data dir, never copied into this file |

title: Add retry to embedding client
branch: feat/embed-retry  # optional
session: 5cc41a6e-9f2c-4c11-b0a6-2f4e7f1d8a33
                          # optional; Claude Code session id of the agent
                          # working this task — the UI shows a button that
                          # copies `claude --resume <session>`
worklog: embed-retry      # optional; worklog ticket id (join key). Shown
                          # as a badge; when the worklog data dir is
                          # mounted, notes/<id>.md renders in a Notes
                          # section (render, never copied)
tier: 2                   # optional; dev-context tier 0-3
complexity: medium        # optional; low|medium|high — uncertainty/blast
                          # radius, throttles fan-out depth (fan-out skill)
type: spike               # optional; epic|spike (mirrored by `worklog
                          # start` from the ticket's Type). `epic` makes
                          # this an epic container — see "Epic files";
                          # `spike` marks investigation-first work, which
                          # the UI renders on the short track
                          # intake|research|present|done. Absent for an
                          # ordinary ticket.
phase: implementing       # optional; intake|clarify|research|contract|plan|
                          # implementing|verify|present|ship|done. A spike
                          # uses the subset intake|research|present|done.

plan:                     # todo list
  - text: Wrap indexer calls in retry decorator
    state: done           # pending|in_progress|done|blocked
  - text: Add backoff tests
    state: in_progress

scorecard:                # contract acceptance criteria, live status
  - text: Retries on connection error, max 3 attempts
    verify: pytest tests/test_retry.py
    status: pass          # pending|pass|fail

decisions:                # implementation decisions + amendments
  - what: Retry lives in indexer, not shared client
    why: Sync path can't tolerate blocking
    when: 2026-09-01

    lines: 88-104
    lang: python
    note: The load-bearing change — exponential backoff, jittered
    snippet: |
      @retry(attempts=3, backoff=exponential(0.5))
      def embed_batch(texts): ...

waiting_on:               # external-answer queue: blocked on OTHER people/teams
  - text: Can platform raise the rate limit for the batch endpoint?
    who: platform-team    # required; who owes the answer
    asked: 2026-09-01     # YYYY-MM-DD; the UI renders age from this
    link: https://slack.example/thread   # where it was asked (optional)
    detail: |
      context the answerer needs
                          # distinct from needs_you (blocked on the task's
                          # own human). Age is independent of any worklog
                          # `Waiting since` stamp. Resolve via
                          # `worklog task waiting-on resolve` — answers are
                          # recorded as decisions and appended to worklog
                          # notes (the ONE sanctioned devboard->worklog
                          # write; mirroring is otherwise one-way).

needs_you:                # attention queue — questions & pending checkpoints
  - type: checkpoint      # question|checkpoint
    text: Commit approval pending
    detail: |
      Summary: retry decorator in indexer.py, 2 new tests. Message:

## Epic files

An epic ticket's file is the single dashboard surface for all of its
children's work — no child of an epic gets its own task file. `type: epic`
marks it; `children` carries one entry per child, in notes-file document
order. An epic file's own `branch`/`session`/`tier`/`complexity`/`phase`/

<child-id>`.

```yaml
schema: 1
type: epic
title: Slim the skills library
worklog: skill-slim
children:
  - id: slim-session-hook
    title: SessionStart hook injects worklog status
    state: active
    branch: feat/slim-hook
    phase: implementing
    plan:
      - text: emit compact orient block as SessionStart JSON
        state: done
    scorecard:
      - text: hook never exits 2
        verify: go test ./internal/hook/...
        status: pass
  - id: slim-eval-harness
    title: Three-way skill eval harness
    state: active
    phase: plan
  - id: slim-dedupe
    title: Cut duplicated devboard-sync and tone content
    state: done
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Devboard: dashboard over a directory of task files.
3	
4	Layout: <DEVBOARD_DATA>/<repo>/<task>.{yaml,yml,json}
5	        <DEVBOARD_DATA>/<repo>/_archive/<task>.yaml   (archived; flagged in API)
6	Endpoints:
7	  /               -> static/index.html
8	  /api/tasks      -> all tasks, parsed, grouped by repo dir, plus the
9	                     global friction log parsed from the worklog mount
10	  /events         -> SSE stream; emits a message whenever the data dir changes
11	  /api/archive    -> POST {repo, id}: move task file into <repo>/_archive/
12	  /api/unarchive  -> POST {repo, id}: move it back
13	
14	The two POST endpoints are the server's only writes, and both are a single
15	validated rename — task content and the worklog dir are never touched.
16	"""
17	
18	import json
19	import os
20	import re
21	import threading
22	import time
23	from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
24	
25	import yaml
26	
27	DATA_DIR = os.environ.get("DEVBOARD_DATA", "/data")
28	WORKLOG_DIR = os.environ.get("DEVBOARD_WORKLOG", "/worklog")  # notes/<id>.md + FEEDBACK.md, read-only
29	PORT = int(os.environ.get("DEVBOARD_PORT", "8484"))
30	SCAN_INTERVAL = float(os.environ.get("DEVBOARD_SCAN_INTERVAL", "1.0"))
31	STATIC_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "static")
32	TASK_EXTS = (".yaml", ".yml", ".json")
33	ARCHIVE_DIR = "_archive"  # per-repo subdir; the only place the server ever moves files
34	FEEDBACK_MD = "FEEDBACK.md"  # friction log at the worklog root; written only by the worklog CLI
35	
36	# Entry heading in FEEDBACK.md: "## <unix-ts> — <signal>" (em dash).
37	FEEDBACK_HEADING = re.compile(r"^## (\d+) \u2014 (\S+)$")
38	
39	_version = 0
40	_changed = threading.Condition()
41	
42	
43	def _snapshot():
44	    """Map of watched-file path -> (mtime, size) for change detection.
45	    Covers task files, worklog notes and FEEDBACK.md, so note edits and
46	    newly captured (or resolved) friction hot-reload too."""
47	    snap = {}
48	    try:
49	        with os.scandir(DATA_DIR) as repos:
50	            for repo in repos:
51	                if not repo.is_dir() or repo.name.startswith("."):
52	                    continue
53	                with os.scandir(repo.path) as files:
54	                    for f in files:
55	                        if f.is_file() and f.name.lower().endswith(TASK_EXTS):
56	                            st = f.stat()
57	                            snap[f.path] = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)
58	                try:
59	                    with os.scandir(os.path.join(repo.path, ARCHIVE_DIR)) as arc:
60	                        for f in arc:
61	                            if f.is_file() and f.name.lower().endswith(TASK_EXTS):
62	                                st = f.stat()
63	                                snap[f.path] = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)
64	                except (FileNotFoundError, NotADirectoryError):
65	                    pass
66	    except FileNotFoundError:
67	        pass
68	    try:
69	        fpath = os.path.join(WORKLOG_DIR, FEEDBACK_MD)
70	        st = os.stat(fpath)
71	        snap[fpath] = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)
72	    except (FileNotFoundError, NotADirectoryError, PermissionError):
73	        pass
74	    try:
75	        with os.scandir(os.path.join(WORKLOG_DIR, "notes")) as notes:
76	            for f in notes:
77	                if f.is_file() and f.name.lower().endswith(".md"):
78	                    st = f.stat()
79	                    snap[f.path] = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)
80	    except (FileNotFoundError, NotADirectoryError, PermissionError):
81	        pass
82	    return snap
83	
84	
85	def _watcher():
86	    global _version
87	    prev = _snapshot()
88	    while True:
89	        time.sleep(SCAN_INTERVAL)
90	        cur = _snapshot()
91	        if cur != prev:
92	            prev = cur
93	            with _changed:
94	                _version += 1
95	                _changed.notify_all()
96	
97	
98	def _parse_task(path, archived=False):
99	    rel = os.path.relpath(path, DATA_DIR)
100	    entry = {"file": rel, "id": os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]}
101	    if archived:
102	        entry["archived"] = True
103	    try:
104	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
105	            raw = fh.read()
106	        data = json.loads(raw) if path.lower().endswith(".json") else yaml.safe_load(raw)
107	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
108	            raise ValueError("top level must be a mapping")
109	        entry["task"] = data
110	        st = os.stat(path)
111	        entry["mtime"] = st.st_mtime
112	        wl = data.get("worklog")
113	        if isinstance(wl, str) and wl and "/" not in wl and ".." not in wl:
114	            np = os.path.join(WORKLOG_DIR, "notes", wl + ".md")
115	            try:
116	                with open(np, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as nf:
117	                    entry["notes"] = nf.read()
118	            except OSError:
119	                pass  # no notes file: section simply absent
120	    except Exception as exc:  # any bad file becomes an error card, never a 500
121	        entry["error"] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
122	    return entry
123	
124	
125	def _parse_feedback():
126	    """Parse FEEDBACK.md into a list of entries, oldest first.
127	
128	    Mirrors the format written by `worklog feedback` (Go:
129	    internal/feedback/feedback.go). Deliberately permissive — an unknown
130	    "**Field**:" line is skipped rather than failing, so the Go side can add
131	    fields without breaking the board. Any read or parse problem yields an
132	    empty list: friction is a side panel and must never take down the page.
133	    """
134	    try:
135	        with open(os.path.join(WORKLOG_DIR, FEEDBACK_MD), "r",
136	                  encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
137	            lines = fh.read().split("\n")
138	    except OSError:
139	        return []
140	
141	    entries, cur, in_excerpt = [], None, False
142	    for line in lines:
143	        m = FEEDBACK_HEADING.match(line)
144	        if m:
145	            if cur:
146	                entries.append(cur)
147	            cur = {"timestamp": int(m.group(1)), "signal": m.group(2),
148	                   "trigger": "", "excerpt": "", "context": "", "resolved": 0}
149	            in_excerpt = False
150	            continue
151	        if cur is None:
152	            continue
153	        if line.startswith("**Trigger**: "):
154	            cur["trigger"] = line[len("**Trigger**: "):]
155	            in_excerpt = False
156	        elif line == "**Excerpt**:":
157	            in_excerpt = True
158	        elif line.startswith("**Context**: "):
159	            cur["context"] = line[len("**Context**: "):]
160	            in_excerpt = False
161	        elif line.startswith("**Resolved**: "):
162	            raw = line[len("**Resolved**: "):].strip()
163	            cur["resolved"] = int(raw) if raw.isdigit() else 0
164	            in_excerpt = False
165	        elif line.startswith("**"):
166	            in_excerpt = False  # unknown field: skip the line, keep the entry
167	        elif in_excerpt:
168	            text = line[2:] if line.startswith("> ") else line
169	            cur["excerpt"] = cur["excerpt"] + "\n" + text if cur["excerpt"] else text
170	    if cur:
171	        entries.append(cur)
172	    for e in entries:
173	        e["excerpt"] = e["excerpt"].strip()
174	    return entries
175	
176	
177	def _all_tasks():
178	    repos = []
179	    try:
180	        names = sorted(
181	            d for d in os.listdir(DATA_DIR)
182	            if not d.startswith(".") and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, d))
183	        )
184	    except FileNotFoundError:
185	        names = []
186	    for name in names:
187	        rdir = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, name)
188	        tasks = [
189	            _parse_task(os.path.join(rdir, f))
190	            for f in sorted(os.listdir(rdir))
191	            if f.lower().endswith(TASK_EXTS) and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(rdir, f))
192	        ]
193	        arcdir = os.path.join(rdir, ARCHIVE_DIR)
194	        if os.path.isdir(arcdir):
195	            tasks += [
196	                _parse_task(os.path.join(arcdir, f), archived=True)
197	                for f in sorted(os.listdir(arcdir))
198	                if f.lower().endswith(TASK_EXTS) and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(arcdir, f))
199	            ]
200	        if tasks:
201	            repos.append({"repo": name, "tasks": tasks})
202	    with _changed:
203	        v = _version
204	    return {"version": v, "generated": time.time(), "repos": repos,
205	            "feedback": _parse_feedback()}
206

208	class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
209	    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
210	
211	    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
212	        pass
213	
214	    def _send(self, code, body, ctype="application/json"):
215	        data = body if isinstance(body, bytes) else body.encode("utf-8")
216	        self.send_response(code)
217	        self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
218	        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
219	        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
220	        self.end_headers()
221	        self.wfile.write(data)
222	
223	    def do_GET(self):
224	        path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
225	        if path in ("/", "/index.html"):
226	            with open(os.path.join(STATIC_DIR, "index.html"), "rb") as fh:
227	                self._send(200, fh.read(), "text/html; charset=utf-8")
228	        elif path == "/api/tasks":
229	            # default=str: YAML yields dates/times json can't serialize natively

  .kind { flex: none; font: 500 .68rem var(--mono); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .06em;

  .kind.question { color: var(--signal); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--signal) 14%, transparent); }
  .kind.checkpoint { color: var(--hold); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--hold) 14%, transparent); }

1	# Devboard
2	
3	A browser dashboard over a directory of task files, so the human
4	can follow agent work without living in terminal scrollback. Agents (or
5	anyone) drop one YAML/JSON file per task into `<data-root>/<repo>/`; the
6	page renders plan todos, the contract scorecard, decisions, code-to-know,
7	a "needs you" attention queue, tier/complexity/worklog badges, and a
8	copy-`claude --resume` button per task (from the `session` field) — and
9	hot-reloads within ~2s of any file change, no refresh needed (SSE,
10	auto-reconnecting).
11	
12	Tasks with a `worklog:` join key also render the ticket's
13	`notes/<id>.md` live from the worklog data dir (second read-only mount) —
14	rendered, never copied, and note edits hot-reload too. That mount also
15	carries `FEEDBACK.md`, rendered as the global Friction panel (see below).
16	
17	The intended writer is the `worklog` CLI (`start`/`done`/`pr` side
18	effects plus the `worklog task` family, including `untrack` to stop
19	tracking a task by deleting only its YAML) — but a hand-dropped
20	schema-valid file is fully supported.
21	
22	## Run
23	
24	```sh
25	cd devboard
26	mkdir -p ~/.local/share/devboard
27	docker compose up --build -d
28	# open http://localhost:8484
29	```
30	
31	Defaults: data dir `~/.local/share/devboard`, port `8484`, worklog dir
32	`~/.local/share/worklog` (for notes rendering). Override with
33	`DEVBOARD_DATA=/path WORKLOG_DATA=/path DEVBOARD_PORT=9000 docker compose
34	up -d`. The worklog mount is read-only — the dashboard can never modify
35	worklog state. The data mount is writable for exactly one operation:
36	archiving (see below).
37	
38	Without Docker: `DEVBOARD_DATA=~/.local/share/devboard python3 server.py`
39	(needs `pyyaml`).
40	
41	## Directory layout
42	
43	```
44	<data-root>/
45	  <repo-name>/          # grouping = directory name
46	    <task-slug>.yaml    # one file per task (.yml/.json also fine)
47	    _archive/           # archived tasks (moved here by the UI; kept on disk)
48	      <task-slug>.yaml
49	```
50	
51	See [schema.md](schema.md) for the task file format (`schema: 1`), and
52	[examples/](examples/) for ready-made files — try it out with:
53	
54	```sh
55	cp -r examples/* ~/.local/share/devboard/
56	```
57	
58	## Archive / un-archive
59	
60	The board's only write action. The archive button (on done cards and in
61	every task's detail view) moves the task's file into `<repo>/_archive/`;
62	archived tasks leave the grid, stats, and attention band and collapse into
63	an "Archived · N" fold with un-archive buttons that move them back. Nothing
64	is ever deleted or rewritten — both endpoints (`POST /api/archive`,
65	`POST /api/unarchive`, JSON body `{"repo", "id"}`) are a single validated
66	rename, and the worklog dir is never touched. There is no auth: anyone who
67	can reach the port can archive/un-archive (reversible by design; the server
68	rejects non-JSON content types and never answers CORS preflights, so a
69	browsing session on another site can't trigger it cross-origin).
70	
71	## Friction panel
72	
73	`FEEDBACK.md` at the root of the worklog mount is the friction log the
74	worklog skill's capture subagent appends to (`worklog feedback append`).
75	The board renders it as a single global band — it is not per-task, so no
76	task-file field is involved:
77	
78	- an unreviewed count in the topbar stats, absent when nothing is outstanding
79	- a collapsed `Friction · N` fold with a count per signal, then the
80	  unresolved entries newest-first (signal, local time, trigger, and a fold
81	  for the excerpt and context)
82	- resolved entries in a `Resolved · N` sub-fold, dimmed
83	
84	Reviewing happens in the CLI, never here: the worklog mount is read-only, so
85	each entry offers a button that copies `worklog feedback resolve <timestamp>`
86	rather than writing anything. Running it adds a `**Resolved**: <unix-ts>`
87	line to that entry, and the board updates over SSE within ~2s.
88	
89	The entry format is owned by the Go side
90	(`worklog/internal/feedback/feedback.go`); `server.py` parses it a second
91	time because the container ships no `worklog` binary. The reader skips
92	unknown `**Field**:` lines rather than failing, so the two can be extended
93	independently. `devboard/test_server.py` (stdlib `unittest`, no extra
94	dependency) pins the reader:
95	
96	```sh
97	cd devboard && python3 -m unittest test_server
98	```
99	
100	## Behavior notes
101	
102	- Malformed files render as an error card (filename + parse error); they
103	  never take down the rest of the page.
104	- Unknown top-level fields render in an "Other" section — extend freely.
105	- Tasks untouched for >2h render dimmed (likely-stale signal).
106	- A missing or malformed `FEEDBACK.md` simply means no friction panel —
107	  it never takes down the page.
108	- Server: Python stdlib + PyYAML; a 1s mtime scan drives the SSE stream
109	  (no inotify — works identically under Docker volume mounts).

hot-reloads within ~2s of any file change, no refresh needed (SSE,
auto-reconnecting).

Tasks with a `worklog:` join key also render the ticket's
`notes/<id>.md` live from the worklog data dir (second read-only mount) —
rendered, never copied, and note edits hot-reload too. That mount also
carries `FEEDBACK.md`, rendered as the global Friction panel (see below).

The intended writer is the `worklog` CLI (`start`/`done`/`pr` side
effects plus the `worklog task` family, including `untrack` to stop
tracking a task by deleting only its YAML) — but a hand-dropped
schema-valid file is fully supported.

## Run

```sh
cd devboard
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/devboard
docker compose up --build -d
# open http://localhost:8484
```

Defaults: data dir `~/.local/share/devboard`, port `8484`, worklog dir
`~/.local/share/worklog` (for notes rendering). Override with
`DEVBOARD_DATA=/path WORKLOG_DATA=/path DEVBOARD_PORT=9000 docker compose
up -d`. The worklog mount is read-only — the dashboard can never modify
worklog state. The data mount is writable for exactly one operation:
archiving (see below).

Without Docker: `DEVBOARD_DATA=~/.local/share/devboard python3 server.py`
(needs `pyyaml`).

## Directory layout

```
<data-root>/
  <repo-name>/          # grouping = directory name
    <task-slug>.yaml    # one file per task (.yml/.json also fine)
    _archive/           # archived tasks (moved here by the UI; kept on disk)
      <task-slug>.yaml
```

See [schema.md](schema.md) for the task file format (`schema: 1`), and
[examples/](examples/) for ready-made files — try it out with:

```sh
cp -r examples/* ~/.local/share/devboard/
```

## Archive / un-archive

The board's only write action. The archive button (on done cards and in
every task's detail view) moves the task's file into `<repo>/_archive/`;
archived tasks leave the grid, stats, and attention band and collapse into
an "Archived · N" fold with un-archive buttons that move them back. Nothing
is ever deleted or rewritten — both endpoints (`POST /api/archive`,
`POST /api/unarchive`, JSON body `{"repo", "id"}`) are a single validated
rename, and the worklog dir is never touched. There is no auth: anyone who
can reach the port can archive/un-archive (reversible by design; the server
rejects non-JSON content types and never answers CORS preflights, so a
browsing session on another site can't trigger it cross-origin).

## Friction panel

`FEEDBACK.md` at the root of the worklog mount is the friction log the
worklog skill's capture subagent appends to (`worklog feedback append`).
The board renders it as a single global band — it is not per-task, so no
task-file field is involved:

- an unreviewed count in the topbar stats, absent when nothing is outstanding
- a collapsed `Friction · N` fold with a count per signal, then the
  unresolved entries newest-first (signal, local time, trigger, and a fold
  for the excerpt and context)
- resolved entries in a `Resolved · N` sub-fold, dimmed

Reviewing happens in the CLI, never here: the worklog mount is read-only, so
each entry offers a button that copies `worklog feedback resolve <timestamp>`
rather than writing anything. Running it adds a `**Resolved**: <unix-ts>`
line to that entry, and the board updates over SSE within ~2s.

The entry format is owned by the Go side
(`worklog/internal/feedback/feedback.go`); `server.py` parses it a second
time because the container ships no `worklog` binary. The reader skips
unknown `**Field**:` lines rather than failing, so the two can be extended
independently. `devboard/test_server.py` (stdlib `unittest`, no extra
dependency) pins the reader:

```sh
cd devboard && python3 -m unittest test_server
```

## Behavior notes

- Malformed files render as an error card (filename + parse error); they
  never take down the rest of the page.
- Unknown top-level fields render in an "Other" section — extend freely.
- Tasks untouched for >2h render dimmed (likely-stale signal).
- A missing or malformed `FEEDBACK.md` simply means no friction panel —
  it never takes down the page.
- Server: Python stdlib + PyYAML; a 1s mtime scan drives the SSE stream
  (no inotify — works identically under Docker volume mounts).

## Findings

**Why the gap exists:** the dashboard (`devboard/server.py`) only ever reads `<DEVBOARD_DATA>/<repo>/*.yaml` task files. Those files are created by `worklog start` → `devboard.OnStart()` (`worklog/internal/devboard/devboard.go:392`), which is the *only* code path that ever creates one. A ticket sitting in `## Next` or `## Someday` in `WORK.md` has never been started, so `OnStart` has never run, so no task file exists, so the dashboard has literally nothing to iterate over for it. This is intentional per `schema.md`'s ownership model ("worklog→devboard only," task files as disposable in-flight telemetry) — it's not a bug, it's a scope gap.

**What's already in place that makes this easy:**
- `server.py` already mounts the worklog data dir read-only as `WORKLOG_DIR` and already parses one file from it directly in Python (`FEEDBACK.md`, via `_parse_feedback()`) rather than shelling out to the `worklog` binary — the README is explicit that this is deliberate: "the container ships no `worklog` binary." `WORK.md` lives at the root of that same mount (`Workdir.WorkMD()`), so reading it needs no new mount, just a new parse function following the same precedent.
- The Go side already exposes exactly the right shape: `worklog status --json` (`internal/cli/status.go`) emits `Now`/`Waiting`/`Next`/`Someday` as structured blocks — `id`, `title`, `type`, `parent`, `repo`, `tags`, `started`, `pr`, `acceptance`, `notesRef`, `activeChildren`, etc. That's a stable, already-versioned contract for exactly this data; the Python parser would just be a lightweight re-implementation of the same `WORK.md` block grammar (`internal/parse/work.go`, `internal/model/block.go`), mirroring how `FEEDBACK.md`'s Go writer and Python reader are already kept in sync independently.
- `_snapshot()` (the mtime-diff loop driving SSE hot-reload) already needs one more `os.stat(WORK.md)` entry to make backlog changes hot-reload too — trivial addition to an existing mechanism.

## Recommendation

Extend `server.py` to parse `WORK.md`'s `## Next` and `## Someday` sections directly (same "duplicate a narrow reader in Python" pattern as `FEEDBACK.md`), and surface them in `/api/tasks` as a separate lightweight list — not as full cards. A Next/Someday ticket has no branch, session, plan, scorecard, or phase, so forcing it through `cardHTML()` would either show a mostly-empty card or invite fields that don't apply yet. Instead:

- Add a `backlog` (or `next`/`someday`) array to the JSON payload, grouped by the block's `Repo` field the same way task files are grouped by directory today.
- Render it as a collapsed band/fold on the board view, same visual language as the existing "Waiting on others" and "Needs you" folds — title, id, type badge (epic/spike/chore), tags, parent — with **no detail page**, since there's no task file to link to. Maybe a "not started" hint or a copy-`worklog start <id>` button, mirroring the existing `resumeBtn`/`copyCmd` affordances.

**Why not the alternative** (have `worklog add`/`edit` write a stub devboard file for every Next/Someday ticket, not just started ones): it multiplies write paths (`add`, `edit`, section-move, `done`, delete-from-WORK.md all now need to keep a stub file in sync) and creates two competing authorities for "is this ticket alive" — WORK.md's section placement vs. a YAML file's presence/phase — which is exactly what schema.md's "one author per field" rule is designed to avoid. Parsing `WORK.md` read-only for display keeps worklog as the sole source of truth and touches zero write paths.

**Scope note:** `## Waiting` tickets already have task files (they were started, then paused), so they're already covered by the existing card rendering — the real gap is only `Next`/`Someday`, matching the ticket title.

Rough size: a `_parse_workmd()` function in `server.py` (~40-60 lines, block-grammar parser) + one `_snapshot()` line + a small `index.html` render function and CSS for the new fold. No Go changes needed at all.
